title: Clopen realization of a base-changed restricted equivalence relation
statement:
Let $T,U,R$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with structure morphisms $U\to T$, $R\to T$, and $T$-morphisms $s,t:R\to U$. Suppose $j=(s,t):R\to U\times_TU$ identifies $R(H)$ with an equivalence relation on $U(H)$ for every $T$-scheme $H$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $B\to T$ be any morphism of schemes. Write $U_B=U\times_TB$, $R_B=R\times_TB$, and $s_B,t_B:R_B\to U_B$ for the induced morphisms. Let $V\subseteq U_B$ be an open and closed subscheme with its induced structure [def-weil-open-immersion]. The subset $s_B^{-1}(V)\cap t_B^{-1}(V)$ is open and closed in $R_B$; let $C$ be its induced open subscheme and let $D$ be its induced open complement. Then $R_B=C\amalg D$, and there are canonical isomorphisms, compatible with the maps to $R_B$ and to both copies of $V$,
$$C\cong V\times_{U_B,s_B}R_B\times_{t_B,U_B}V\cong (V\times_BV)\times_{U\times_TU}R.$$
For every $B$-scheme $H$, composition with $V\hookrightarrow U_B$ identifies $V(H)$ with a subset of $U_B(H)=U(H)$ (the last equality is relative to the fixed map $H\to B\to T$), and identifies $C(H)$ with exactly the pairs in $R(H)$ whose two endpoints belong to this subset. In particular the two induced maps $C\rightrightarrows V$ form an equivalence relation on $H$-points for every $B$-scheme $H$.

source.place: Tag 02VD (lemma-restrict-groupoid-relation), with arbitrary base change and the induced clopen open-subscheme realization; specialization used in more-groupoids.tex Tag 03X5 (lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper), conclusion (h).

proof.text: Put $X=U_B$, $Y=R_B$, and $W=s_B^{-1}(|V|)\cap t_B^{-1}(|V|)$. Morphisms of schemes are continuous. Each inverse image is open and closed because $|V|$ is, so $W$ and its complement are open and closed. Thus the induced open subschemes $C=Y|_W$ and $D=Y|_{Y\setminus W}$ have disjoint images covering $Y$. Their structure sheaves are precisely the restrictions of $\mathcal O_Y$, as specified by the induced open-subscheme structure.

source.place: Tag 03X5 (lemma-quasi-finite-over-base-j-proper), clopen inverse-image decomposition in the proof

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], form $E=C\amalg D$ and the map $f:E\to Y$ induced by the two inclusions. Glue the two coprojections $C\to E$ and $D\to E$ over the disjoint open covering $Y=C\cup D$, using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], to obtain $g:Y\to E$. The composites $fg$ and $\operatorname{id}_Y$ agree on $C,D$, so are equal by uniqueness of gluing. The composites $gf$ and $\operatorname{id}_E$ agree after both coprojections, so are equal by the coproduct universal property. This proves the asserted decomposition as schemes.

source.place: Tags 01JB (lemma-glue) and 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes), disjoint gluing and mapping property

proof.text: Let $i:C\hookrightarrow Y$ and $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusions. The images of $s_Bi$ and $t_Bi$ lie in $V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] they factor uniquely as $va=s_Bi$, $vb=t_Bi$, with $a,b:C\to V$. More generally a morphism $r:H\to Y$ factors uniquely through $C$ exactly when both $s_Br$ and $t_Br$ factor through $V$: in the forward direction compose $a,b$ with the factor through $C$; in the reverse direction the endpoint factorizations imply $|r|(H)\subseteq W$, and the cited open-factorization statement applies to $C\subseteq Y$. All these factorizations are over $B$, by composing the defining equalities with the structure morphism.

source.place: Tag 01HI (lemma-restrict-map-to-opens), applied to the two endpoint maps and to the clopen intersection

proof.text: Let $P=V\times_{X,s_B}Y\times_{t_B,X}V$. The maps $(a,i,b)$ define $k:C\to P$ by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write its three projections as $p_1,p_Y,p_2$. They satisfy $vp_1=s_Bp_Y$ and $vp_2=t_Bp_Y$, so step 3 gives a unique $l:P\to C$ with $il=p_Y$. Now $ilk=i$, so $lk=\operatorname{id}_C$ by uniqueness of factorization through $C$. Moreover $val=vp_1$ and $vbl=vp_2$; cancellation of the open immersion $v$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism] gives $al=p_1$, $bl=p_2$. Thus $kl$ has the same three projections as $\operatorname{id}_P$ and equals it by the iterated fibre-product universal property. This is the first canonical isomorphism, preserving the map to $Y$ and both endpoint maps to $V$.

source.place: Tag 02VD (lemma-restrict-groupoid-relation), iterated restriction square; explicit universal-property verification

proof.text: Put $Q=(V\times_BV)\times_{U\times_TU}R$. Denote its projections to $V$ by $q_1,q_2$ and to $R$ by $r$. Their equalities are $v_Uq_1=sr$, $v_Uq_2=tr$ and $b_Vq_1=b_Vq_2$, where $v_U:V\to U$ and $b_V:V\to B$ are the projections of $v$. Hence $(r,b_Vq_1)$ determines $q_Y:Q\to Y=R\times_TB$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The maps $s_Bq_Y$ and $vq_1$ agree after both projections of $X=U\times_TB$, and therefore agree; likewise $t_Bq_Y=vq_2$. Thus $(q_1,q_Y,q_2)$ defines $Q\to P$. Conversely the projections of $P$ give $(p_1,p_2):P\to V\times_BV$ (their $B$-coordinates both equal that of $p_Y$) and $p_R:P\to R$. The endpoint equalities give their common map to $U\times_TU$, so they define $P\to Q$. Both composites fix all the named projections and hence are identities by the fibre-product universal property. This proves $P\cong Q$. Its map to $Y$ is the displayed pair $(r,b_Vq_1)$, so the isomorphism preserves the specified map to $R_B$ as well as both maps to $V$.

source.place: Tag 02VD (lemma-restrict-groupoid-relation), displayed Cartesian description; arbitrary base change checked by projections

proof.text: Fix a $B$-scheme $H$ with structural map $h:H\to B$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_B(H,U_B)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_T(H,U)$ by $u\mapsto(u,h)$, and likewise identifies $R_B(H)$ with $R(H)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], composition with $v$ is injective on $H$-points. Step 3 says exactly that $C(H)$ consists of those $r\in R(H)$ whose two endpoints belong to this image of $V(H)$. The hypothesis identifies $R(H)$ injectively with an equivalence relation on $U(H)$. Its restriction to the subset $V(H)$ is reflexive since each $(x,x)$ belongs to the original relation, symmetric since $(x,y)$ implies $(y,x)$, and transitive since $(x,y),(y,z)$ imply $(x,z)$; all the endpoints still belong to that subset. Injectivity of $C(H)\to V(H)\times V(H)$ follows from injectivity for $R(H)$ and uniqueness of factorization through $C$. This proves every pointwise assertion without a groupoid or invariance hypothesis on $V$.
